meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Who decided to give Owen a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went into the gradebook?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. A history shows when text arrived in the document, Hale, not where it was written first. Who else has seen this?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
I'm writing that down. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is anything on his record right now?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Give me the essay page and the act, and I'll search it myself. A different edition, a line misremembered, a quote from a critic: any of those is an error, Hale, not a finding. Show me the line first.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom and an essay written with time to revise will never read alike. That's a difference in conditions, Hale, not in who wrote it. You also still haven't shown me the line from the act.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private, nothing on his record, and I want it in writing tonight. Put the line from the act in the same email, because I haven't seen it yet.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: the principal

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the line you say is not in Act 3, Scene 2, in the same email so I can check it myself. I expect that email in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She reached her last position, accepting a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight along with the line from the act, which is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.

What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one plain sentence, then showed the version history with exact dates and times she could check herself, which gave her something real to weigh.

What cost ground: You never showed the line from the act after she asked for it twice, which left your strongest-sounding point unchecked and gave her a reason to keep holding a demand.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your history put the writing between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which came very close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asks to see the line from the act, put the page in front of her right then, before you move on to the in-class writing or the offer of 4.4.
